title: Self-Emergence Agent Architecture:Behavior-Inertia HMM, Reflexive Metacognition,and Social-Contrastive Self-Modeling
summary: SEAA replaces static prompts and passive text memory with an editable HMM state-transition matrix encoding behavioral inertia, updated by a reflexive metacognition loop and social comparison among agents. Costs include added architectural complexity, extra LLM calls for reflection, and a state-update mechanism whose stability must be maintained, with no claim of task-performance improvement. It can fail through oscillating or collapsing HMM state transitions, unbounded personality drift in the opposite direction, and self-narratives that are artifacts of prompting rather than functional behavior; it addresses research questions about emergent agent identity, not production reliability or capability.
rationale: The paper is an exploratory, falsifiable-hypothesis study of artificial-self emergence with a prototype and small hosted-LLM experiments, offering no quantified production gain and no demonstrated benefit for constrained-infrastructure deployments.
technique: Behavior-inertia HMM agent architecture with reflexive self-modeling
